title: 9.2.0: Exercises
originalText:
For the following exercises, determine the most reasonable value for each area.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)

kitchen floor: 16 km^(2), 16 m^(2), 16 cm^(2), or 16 mm^(2)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{2}\)

national Park: 1,000 km^(2), 1,000 m^(2), 1,000 cm^(2), or 1,000 mm^(2)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{3}\)

classroom table: 5 km^(2), 5 m^(2), 5 cm^(2), or 5 mm^(2)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{4}\)

window: 9,000 km^(2), 9,000 m^(2), 9,000 cm^(2), or 9,000 mm^(2)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{5}\)

paper napkin: 10,000 km^(2), 10,000 m^(2), 10,000 cm^(2), or 10,000 mm^(2)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{6}\)

parking lot: 45,000 km^(2), 45,000 m^(2), 45,000 cm^(2), or 45,000 mm^(2)

For the following exercises, convert the given area to the units shown.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{7}\)

\(700,000\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{8}\)

\(24 \mathrm{~m}^2= \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, \mathrm{cm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{9}\)

\(985 \mathrm{~cm}^2= \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,\mathrm{mm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{10}\)

\(4 \mathrm{~km}^2= \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,\mathrm{m}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{11}\)

\(0.00005 \mathrm{~km}^2= \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, \mathrm{cm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{12}\)

\(68,500,000{\text{ m}}{{\text{m}}^2} = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{13}\)

\(34.5 \mathrm{~m}^2= \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, \mathrm{cm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{14}\)

\(7,800{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} =  \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, {{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{15}\)

\(34.5 \mathrm{~m}^2=\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, \mathrm{cm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{16}\)

\(0.05{\text{ k}}{{\text{m}}^2} = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{17}\)

\(0.073 \mathrm{~m}^2=\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\, \mathrm{mm}^2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{18}\)

\(27,750{\text{ m}}{{\text{m}}^2} = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

For the following exercises, determine the area.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{19}\)

\(l = 300\) cm, \(w = 4\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{20}\)

\(l = 3,500\) mm, \(w = 0.5\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{21}\)

\(l = 5.5\) km, \(w = 2,750\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{k}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{22}\)

\(l = 2,400\) cm, \(w = 3.2\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{23}\)

\(l = 7\) cm, \(w = 400\) mm

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{24}\)

\(l = 2,300\) m, \(w = 4\) km

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{k}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{25}\)

\(l = 4.2\) cm, \(w = 320\) mm

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{26}\)

\(l = 5,350\) mm, \(w = 0.5\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{27}\)

\(l = 1.8\) km, \(w = 2,300\) m

\(A = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\,{\text{k}}{{\text{m}}^2}\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{28}\)

A notebook is 200 mm by 300 mm. A sticker on the notebook cover measures 2 cm by 2 cm. How many square centimeters of the notebook cover is still visible?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{29}\)

A bedroom wall is 4 m by 2.5 m. A window on the wall is 1 m by 2 m. How much wallpaper is needed to cover the wall?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{30}\)

A wall is 5 m by 2.5 m. A picture hangs on the wall that is 600 mm by 300 mm. How much of the wall, in m^(2), is not covered by the picture?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{31}\)

What is the area of the shape that is shown?

[Figure: An L-shaped figure. The sides measure 7 centimeters, 4 centimeters, 1 centimeter, 3 centimeters, 6 centimeters, and 1 centimeter.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{32}\)

A quilter made a design using a small square, a medium square, and a large square. What is the area of the shaded parts of the design that is shown?

[Figure: Three concentric squares. The sides of the large square measure 16 centimeters. The sides of the medium square measure 14 centimeters. The sides of the small square measure 4 centimeters. The small square is shaded. The region between the medium and large squares is shaded.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{33}\)

A landscaper makes a plan for a walkway in a backyard, as shown. How many square meters of patio brick does the landscaper need to cover the walkway?

[Figure: An L-shaped figure. The sides measure 2 meters, 4 meters, 9 meters, 1.5 meters, 7 meters, and 2.5 meters.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{34}\)

A painter completed a portrait. The height of the portrait is 36 cm. The width is half as long as the height. What is the area of the portrait in square meters?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{35}\)

A room has an area of 137.5 m^(2). The length of the room is 11 m. What is the width of the room?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{36}\)

A wall is 4.5 m long by 3 m high. A can of paint will cover an area of 10 m^(2). How many cans of paint are needed if each wall needs 2 coats of paint?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{37}\)

A soccer field is 110 meters long and 75 meters wide. If the cost of artificial turf is $30 per square meter, what is the cost of covering the soccer field with artificial turf?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{38}\)

A window is 150 centimeters wide and 90 centimeters high. If three times the area of the window is needed for curtain material, how much curtain material is needed in square meters?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{39}\)

A rectangular flower garden is 5.5 meters wide and 8.4 meters long. A path with a width of 1 meter is laid around the garden. What is the area of the path?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{40}\)

A dining room is 8 meters wide by 6 meters long. Wood flooring costs $12.50 per square meter. How much will it costs to install wood flooring in the dining room?
